name: Calixto Yamamura-Abioye
subcategory: rising star / SYNAPSE SLAM CONTINENTAL neural-physical hybrid
description: A nineteen-year-old Filipino-Yoruba prodigy from Meridian's Tier 3 central district who entered the SYNAPSE SLAM CONTINENTAL circuit in 2222 and by 2223 had reached the semi-finals with a BCI-physical integration score that the league's technical committee called 'statistically unprecedented for an athlete under twenty-five.' His style — fluid, economical, almost meditative in its pacing against opponents who favor aggressive neural bursting — has generated enormous broadcast interest and a wave of academic papers on developmental BCI integration. He is famously quiet off the circuit, gives sparse interviews, and lives with his grandmother in the same Tier 3 apartment block where he grew up.
story_hooks: Someone is attempting to steal Yamamura-Abioye's neural performance data before Axiom can fully archive it — and the theft attempt suggests a rival corponation intelligence operation rather than a lone hacker.

A SYNAPSE SLAM opponent who lost to Yamamura-Abioye in a high-stakes semi-final is hospitalized with an unexplained BCI cascade injury, and the pattern of the cascade matches the specific neural signature Yamamura-Abioye deploys in his signature finishing sequence.

Yamamura-Abioye quietly approaches an independent legal advocate about the data rights clause in his Axiom contract — and the advocate discovers the clause may be part of a broader Axiom initiative to harvest developmental BCI data from a cohort of young athletes signed under similar terms.
